correctness.rationale: For a fixed interleaving pattern of at most nk atoms, the probability law is a polynomial image of at most n(k-1) free masses; finitely many patterns give the upper bound. For n>=4, explicit patterns give n or 2n distinct nonidentity one-atom-deviation permutations, hence the Jacobian columns e_sigma-e_id are independent at the all-baseline boundary. Polynomial persistence gives a strictly positive interior point of identical rank; the inverse-function criterion proves matching lower bounds. Exact checker reconstructed all listed finite witnesses through n=100 and verified an independent 3-label rational determinant, with its finite scope distinguished from the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-order bounded-support dimensions for k=2 and k=3 are posed as unknown by Turvey 2026, Section 6 Problem 2. Turvey obtains only the unrestricted dimension, and Babson et al. obtain an unrestricted bound plus small-n examples. The n=3 ternary saturation is already implicit in Babson et al. and is explicitly excluded from the new claim; neither source gives the explicit 2n single-deviation Jacobian certificate for all n>=4. published-finding corpus comparisons identified nearby rank-distribution results but not a covering theorem. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: No independent historical-priority validation; broader literature on finite dice, random utility and ranking-law dimension may contain an equivalent theorem under alternative language.

value.rationale: A 2026 primary paper explicitly asks for semialgebraic dimensions under each support budget. The result settles the first two nontrivial support budgets simultaneously for every n>=4, proving that full intrinsic mass-parameter dimension survives the nonlinear ranking map. This gives a natural model-complexity frontier for finite independent random utilities/dice rather than an arbitrary small numerical table, and includes explicit full-rank realizations useful for further geometric analysis.
